messages:
incident-bot: Pager: PROD HIGH - multiple 5xx errors observed on inference-service during canary deploy (deploy id: deploy-2026-03-15-09). Alerting on p50/p95 spikes and increased error rate :rotating_light:

anne: I see spikes in 502 and KMS Decrypt errors in the logs. Seems tied to the new KMS key we rolled into the canary.

anne: log excerpt:```
2026-03-15T09:02:41Z inference-service ERROR request_id=abc123 KMSDecryptionError: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:iam::1111:role/inference-executor is not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:1111:key/NEW-ROTATED-KEY

stack: /srv/runtime/kms_client.py:142 -> /srv/runtime/inference.py:87
```

maria: confirmed. The canary was supposed to use the rotated key but the IAM role on the canary nodes doesn't have kms:Decrypt for the new key. Might be an env var pointing at the new key id.

raj: omg that matches the deploy change. We flipped KMS_KEY_ID in the canary env during the rollout. Canary traffic is 10% but errors propagate to upstream router -> 5xx for some customers.

beth: customer-impact check: Support reported 3 incidents from enterprise accounts (org-42, org-77) — they see intermittent failures when calling the hosted endpoint. ETA of customers being affected unknown, but error rate hit 8% at peak.

support-eng: seeing spikes on region us-west-2 only, requests that hit canary path failing. Non-canary nodes fine.

anne: immediate mitigation: kill the feature flag that sent traffic to the canary OR rollback the canary. Which is faster?

maria: kill the FF is quickest. Feature flag is ff.kms_new_key_enabled. Flip it to off and we stop sending traffic to canary.

raj: I can rollback the deployment too, but that will take ~5-7 minutes plus CI gating. Let's kill the flag first.

raj: @maria can you flip the flag? I will prepare rollback in parallel.

maria: flipping flag now via LaunchDarkly API...```bash
curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $LD_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://app.launchdarkly.com/api/v2/flags/redwood/inference/ff.kms_new_key_enabled \
  -d '{"environments": {"production": {"on": false}}}'
```

maria: flipped to off. Confirmed in UI -> percentage to canary = 0%.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollback triggered by raj (rollback id: rb-2310009876). Status: rollbacks started across 3 canary nodes.

oncall-sre: taking ownership of incident. I'll watch metrics and confirm error rate drops. Handing off from anne.

oncall-sre: p50 latency back to normal in us-west-2, error rate down from 8% -> 0.6% over last 90s.

support-eng: notifying affected customers: sent templated message to org-42 and org-77 with brief outage note and mitigation steps.

anne: root cause summary so far: KMS key rotation was deployed to canary without updating IAM permissions for the canary execution role. When the canary received traffic it attempted to use the new key and failed Decrypt -> returned 5xx.

beth: product/CS note: need to track customers impacted and follow-up ramp credits and postmortem.

raj: action items: (1) verify IAM role on canary nodes includes kms:Decrypt for new key (2) add deploy-time guard that ensures KMS_KEY_ID has corresponding IAM binding or fails fast (3) add post-deploy smoke to test key usage on canary path.

maria: I'll run a quick audit on the key policy and update the CloudFormation template so role binding is added. Also adding a preflight CI check to validate key policy -> role mapping.

oncall-sre: leaving incident channel but still oncall for followups. We'll open postmortem ticket and assign owners.

anne: thanks everyone. I'll file the incident and include logs + timeline. Marking as mitigated for now. :white_check_mark:
